cases.title: Zinc hydroxide precipitates, then dissolves in excess base
cases.original_forecast: A moderate hydroxide dose gives Zn(OH)2; sufficiently strong excess hydroxide can redissolve it into soluble hydroxo-zinc species.

original_expected_processes.interpretation: Educational chemical equation, not an assertion that the runtime implements every species or pathway.

cases.script:
# PR-001: Zinc hydroxide precipitates, then dissolves in excess base
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 ZnSO4 0.001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.002mol
inspect v1
add v1 NaOH 0.008mol
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
inspect

criteria.criterion: A zinc-bearing hydroxide solid appears at the intermediate snapshot.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/5: Zn(OH)2 solid falls from 0.0009992239624 to 0.0009743391348 mol. Aqueous Zn rises from 7.76037646e-7 to 2.566086517e-5 mol; total Zn is 0.001 mol to floating-point residual. Final Zn(OH)4-2 and Zn(OH)3- molalities are 0.0001647 and 0.00008884. This supports a small decrease (about 2.49% of intermediate solid), not complete clearing.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: No unsupported-hydroxo escape is used. No full dissolution yield, calibrated spectrum or complete heat claim.

criteria.criterion: Its amount decreases after excess base while total zinc remains constant; unsupported hydroxo-complex coverage is not a chemical pass.

cases.title: Dissolve magnesium hydroxide and reprecipitate it
cases.original_forecast: Acid dissolves the initial hydroxide; restoring alkalinity produces a magnesium hydroxide solid again without inventing a magnesium-chloride bottle key.

original_expected_processes.interpretation: Educational chemical equation, not an assertion that the runtime implements every species or pathway.

cases.script:
# PR-002: Dissolve magnesium hydroxide and reprecipitate it
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 Mg(OH)2 0.001mol
inspect v1
add v1 HCl 0.002mol
inspect v1
add v1 NaOH 0.002mol
inspect v1

criteria.criterion: The solid inventory falls on acidification and rises again after base addition.
criteria.observations: Rows 2/4/6: Mg(OH)2 solid 0.0009867943731 -> 0 -> 0.0009835919635 mol. Aqueous Mg 0.00001320562691 -> 0.001 -> 0.00001640803648 mol. The phase sums retain the original 0.001 mol magnesium within recorded floating-point residual.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: Exact numerical residuals remain in the snapshots; no new acceptance tolerance is introduced.

criteria.criterion: Total magnesium stays at 0.001 mol across the cycle.

cases.title: Ferric hydroxide redissolves when its pH support is removed
cases.original_forecast: Brown ferric hydroxide formed by base addition is substantially removed by a deliberate excess of acid.

original_expected_processes.interpretation: Educational chemical equation, not an assertion that the runtime implements every species or pathway.

cases.script:
# PR-003: Ferric hydroxide redissolves when its pH support is removed
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 FeCl3 0.001mol
add v1 NaOH 0.003mol
inspect v1
add v1 HCl 0.006mol
inspect v1
measure v1 ph
inspect

criteria.criterion: Ferric solid decreases after the acid challenge.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/5: Fe(OH)3 solid 0.0009999958515 -> 0 mol; final aqueous Fe+3 analytical total 0.001 mol and pH 1.59949280306. Initial dissolved Fe 4.148537473e-9 mol. Dissolved ownership, rather than appearance, establishes iron retention.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: No claim of a new pure iron salt bottle or free Fe3+ concentration from the analytical carrier.

criteria.criterion: Iron remains in the vessel in dissolved forms; disappearance of turbidity is not disappearance of iron.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/5: Fe(OH)3 solid 0.0009999958515 -> 0 mol; final aqueous Fe+3 analytical total 0.001 mol and pH 1.59949280306. Initial dissolved Fe 4.148537473e-9 mol. Dissolved ownership, rather than appearance, establishes iron retention.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: No claim of a new pure iron salt bottle or free Fe3+ concentration from the analytical carrier.

cases.title: An acid reserve can prevent calcium carbonate precipitation
cases.original_forecast: Without prior acid, carbonate precipitates calcium. With excess proton capacity, carbonate is protonated and the calcium mostly remains dissolved.
cases.script:
# PR-006: An acid reserve can prevent calcium carbonate precipitation
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CaCl2 0.001mol
add v1 Na2CO3 0.001mol
inspect v1
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 HCl 0.003mol
add v2 CaCl2 0.001mol
add v2 Na2CO3 0.001mol
inspect v2

criteria.criterion: The unacidified vessel has more calcium-carbonate solid.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/9: neutral CaCO3 solid 0.0009826363956 mol versus acidified solid 0. Final acidified dissolved Ca 0.001 mol. Added HCl 0.003 mol; final analytical H+ 0.0010000000846 mol, consistent with approximately 0.002 mol proton consumption. Row 8 CO2 gas_evolved exports 0.0009986985126323 mol; remaining aqueous carbon plus this export is 0.0010000000000000002 mol.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: Gas_evolved in the open boundary is an export, not retained headspace inventory; count the event once, not at every later inspect. Carbon quantities are explicitly partitioned, not inferred from lost vessel mass.

criteria.criterion: Account for acid consumption and carbon leaving the open acidified vessel as CO2.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/9: neutral CaCO3 solid 0.0009826363956 mol versus acidified solid 0. Final acidified dissolved Ca 0.001 mol. Added HCl 0.003 mol; final analytical H+ 0.0010000000846 mol, consistent with approximately 0.002 mol proton consumption. Row 8 CO2 gas_evolved exports 0.0009986985126323 mol; remaining aqueous carbon plus this export is 0.0010000000000000002 mol.

# PR-007: Limewater clouds and then clears under excess carbon dioxide
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3

add v1 CO2 0.0005mol

add v1 CO2 0.005mol

# PR-014: Purify impure limestone by dissolution and reprecipitation
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CaCO3 0.001mol
add v1 SiO2 0.1g
add v1 HCl 0.002mol
new
filter v1 v2
inspect
add v2 Na2CO3 0.001mol
inspect v2

criteria.criterion: Most SiO2 remains in v1 during filtration.
criteria.observations: Filter row 5: v1 solid SiO2 0.001644364588 mol, v2 dissolved SiO2 0.00001997200777 mol; about 98.8000% of represented Si remains in source. criteria.qualification_or_gap: The receiver has dissolved silica impurity: do not label the recovered material analytically pure or equate gross mass to calcium recovery. Both vessel boundaries are retained.

# PR-004: Excess ammonia can dissolve a copper hydroxide precipitate
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
seal v1 500mL
add v1 CuSO4 0.0005mol
add v1 NaOH 0.001mol
inspect v1
add v1 NH3 0.05mol
inspect v1
measure v1 uvvis
inspect

All-phase Cu totals 0.0004999999999932997 -> 0.0004999999999932837 mol. Final aqueous analytical NH3 + NH4+ plus gas NH3 = 0.05000000000000062 mol; the gas share is 0.0001784815665 mol. Initial headspace N2 is retained separately and was not added as ammonia.

cases.title: Selective hydroxide precipitation separates ferric and cupric ions
cases.original_forecast: A moderately acidic endpoint should preferentially remove ferric hydroxide while leaving much more copper in the filtrate.
cases.script:
# PR-005: Selective hydroxide precipitation separates ferric and cupric ions
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 HCl 0.002mol
add v1 FeCl3 0.0002mol
add v1 CuSO4 0.0002mol
titrate v1 NaOH 0.1M 0.1mL until ph 4 max 400
inspect v1
new
filter v1 v2
inspect

criteria.criterion: At the recorded endpoint, compare fractions of each metal in solid and dissolved pools.
criteria.observations: Rows 4/5 endpoint pH 3.999992675794: dissolved Fe+2 + Fe+3 = 0.0002 mol and Cu = 0.0002 mol; neither has represented solid. Filter row 7 leaves both source fractions zero and transfers both metal totals to v2. Thus Fe retained fraction 0 does not exceed Cu retained fraction 0.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: The intended selective precipitation is not achieved. Named endpoint diagnostics exclude Fe(OH)3(a) despite SI +1.7 and other iron phases; missing phase selection/ownership is a model gap, not endpoint overshoot. C1 is the requested comparison, not a selective-separation pass.

reason.en: the supplied inventory has uncompensated ionic charge. This adapter interprets non-H/O element totals as an analytical component problem and adjusts pH to impose electroneutrality; H/O basis entries are conservation coordinates, not prescribed free-ion concentrations. A reported pH or speciation therefore describes that proton-compensated analytical problem, not a prediction for a complete physical mixture of these ions. Supply the actual counterions or use complete acid, base or salt reagents; no sodium, chloride or other counterion is inferred

cases.title: Carbonate and sulfate precipitates respond differently to acid
cases.original_forecast: Barium carbonate is acid-labile and can release CO2; barium sulfate should largely persist under the same dilute-acid challenge.
cases.script:
# PR-008: Carbonate and sulfate precipitates respond differently to acid
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 BaCl2 0.0005mol
add v1 Na2CO3 0.0005mol
inspect v1
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 BaCl2 0.0005mol
add v2 Na2SO4 0.0005mol
inspect v2
add v1 HCl 0.002mol
add v2 HCl 0.002mol
inspect

criteria.criterion: First verify formation of each intended solid, including any witherite phase representation.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/8: no BaCO3 solid in carbonate vessel; Ba remains 0.0005 mol aqueous. Sulfate vessel contains 0.0004984214374 mol BaSO4. After acid, BaSO4 is 0.0004971799529 mol, loss about 0.2491%; carbonate solid has no initial amount from which dissolution could be assessed.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: Row 2 explicitly reports Witherite SI +3.0 with no registry solid. CO2 export 0.0004986843358451 mol proves acid action on dissolved carbonate only; it cannot demonstrate dissolution of absent BaCO3.

criteria.criterion: After acid addition, compare each solid with its own initial amount; carbonate loss should greatly exceed sulfate loss.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/8: no BaCO3 solid in carbonate vessel; Ba remains 0.0005 mol aqueous. Sulfate vessel contains 0.0004984214374 mol BaSO4. After acid, BaSO4 is 0.0004971799529 mol, loss about 0.2491%; carbonate solid has no initial amount from which dissolution could be assessed.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: Row 2 explicitly reports Witherite SI +3.0 with no registry solid. CO2 export 0.0004986843358451 mol proves acid action on dissolved carbonate only; it cannot demonstrate dissolution of absent BaCO3.

cases.title: Not every alkaline-earth sulfate precipitates at the same concentration
cases.original_forecast: At these dilute analytical loadings, calcium sulfate is expected to remain mostly dissolved whereas barium sulfate precipitates strongly.
cases.script:
# PR-009: Not every alkaline-earth sulfate precipitates at the same concentration
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 1000mL
add v1 CaCl2 0.001mol
add v1 Na2SO4 0.001mol
inspect v1
new
add v2 water 1000mL
add v2 BaCl2 0.001mol
add v2 Na2SO4 0.001mol
inspect v2

criteria.criterion: The barium vessel has a much larger fraction of its alkaline-earth metal in a sulfate solid.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/8: CaSO4 solid absent, dissolved Ca and sulfate each 0.001 mol. BaSO4 solid 0.0009873155095 mol, about 98.73155% of added barium, with 0.00001268449048 mol dissolved Ba and sulfate each. Dissolved calcium and sulfate ownership is explicit.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: Comparison concerns these specified dilute loadings and represented phases, not all alkaline-earth salts or a kinetic crystallization prediction.

criteria.criterion: A clear calcium solution is not evidence that calcium and sulfate were omitted from its dissolved inventory.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/8: CaSO4 solid absent, dissolved Ca and sulfate each 0.001 mol. BaSO4 solid 0.0009873155095 mol, about 98.73155% of added barium, with 0.00001268449048 mol dissolved Ba and sulfate each. Dissolved calcium and sulfate ownership is explicit.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: Comparison concerns these specified dilute loadings and represented phases, not all alkaline-earth salts or a kinetic crystallization prediction.

cases.title: Solvent identity changes the route to a silver-chloride precipitate
cases.original_forecast: AgCl formation in water uses aqueous speciation, whereas the documented pure-ethanol route is constrained by dissolved reagent fractions and a curated metathesis rule.
cases.script:
# PR-016: Solvent identity changes the route to a silver-chloride precipitate
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 50mL
add v1 AgNO3 0.001mol
add v1 NaCl 0.001mol
inspect v1
new
add v2 ethanol 50mL
add v2 AgNO3 0.001mol
add v2 NaCl 0.001mol
inspect v2

criteria.criterion: Check for AgCl in both systems and explicitly distinguish undissolved starting salt from precipitated product.
criteria.observations: Rows 3/8: aqueous-route AgCl solid 0.0009992088475 mol (99.92088475% of Ag dose); ethanol-route AgCl solid 0.000556097394 mol (55.6097394%). Ethanol contains residual AgNO3 and NaCl, each 0.000443902606 mol labelled liquid, and NaNO3 solid 0.000556097394 mol. Neither starting salt is recorded as an undissolved solid in the final ethanol snapshot.
criteria.qualification_or_gap: Report actual phase labels: the residual reagent is liquid-labelled, not invented undissolved solid. Solvent route is a curated metathesis model, not a validated equal-yield or generic nonaqueous equilibrium claim.

criteria.criterion: Report actual conversion instead of assuming equal yields merely because equal formula amounts were added.
